title: Compact-support Künneth
statement:
For separated finite-type maps $a:X\to S$ and $b:Y\to S$,
with $c:X\times_SY\to S$, and bounded constructible field-coefficient
complexes $K,L$, there is a canonical isomorphism

$$
 Ra_!K\otimes Rb_!L
       \simeq Rc_!(K\boxtimes_SL).
$$

Over a point, this is the Künneth isomorphism for cohomology with
compact support. It respects Weil structures and, for smooth maps, the
trace maps for cohomology with compact support.

*Complement.* The isomorphism is the inverse of the relative Künneth map
$\kappa^{\mathrm{rel}}_{K,L}$ of [sk-thm-sf-kunneth-relative] for $B=S$, and
so has the coherences recorded there (symmetry, triple products, base change).

proof.text:
Let $u:X\times_SY\to X$ and $v:X\times_SY\to Y$ be the projections.
By proper base change ([sk-prop-sf-cbc]), $Ru_!v^*L\simeq a^*Rb_!L$. Applying
the projection formula ([sk-thm-sf-package]) first to $u$ and then to $a$, we
get

$$
 Rc_!(u^*K\otimes v^*L)
  \simeq Ra_!(K\otimes a^*Rb_!L)
  \simeq Ra_!K\otimes Rb_!L.
$$

This isomorphism is natural and compatible with Weil structures
([sk-def-sf-weil-complexes]), because base change and the projection formula
are. For smooth maps, the compatibility with traces ([sk-def-sp-trace])
follows from the composition law for the counits
([sk-prop-sp-trace-composition]), together with the base change of the
purity isomorphism ([sk-prop-sp-purity-bc]).
